title: No test proves a window stop leaves in-flight sibling attempts alone; a teardown-all mutant passes
body: When one tick's refusal stops a width>1 dispatch window, runPlan calls announceAbandoned and must leave the live siblings' worktree, branch and credential untouched so a resumed run can adopt them (window.go). Mutating announceAbandoned to r.tearDown(fl.handle, fl.executor, fl.marker, "mutant", false) for every live sibling passes the whole internal/reconcile suite (-short -count=1, ok 561s): TestARefusalStopsTheWindowAndNamesWhatIsStillRunning checks only that a2 was not integrated and the feed said 'still running'. Add assertions (worktree still registered, branch still present, attempt not cancelled) and ideally a resume that adopts a2, so 'a refusal tears down no more than it should' is falsifiable.
